repo_description: Proof and publication materials for a logarithmic local-memory termination tax in anonymous dynamic binary consensus.
title: A Logarithmic Local-Memory Tax for Explicitly Terminating Binary Consensus in Anonymous Dynamic Networks
abstract: We study deterministic binary consensus in anonymous synchronous 1-interval-connected dynamic networks under one-bit broadcast-counting communication. Stabilizing binary consensus is achievable with one bit of local state without knowledge of the network size. For explicit termination, a split-cycle indistinguishability argument and a finite-state pumping argument imply an Omega(log n) local-memory lower bound. If n is known as a non-uniform algorithm parameter, the lower bound is tight: flooding for n-1 rounds followed by halting uses O(log n) local memory. Thus, in the known-size regime, explicit termination incurs a tight logarithmic local-memory tax relative to stabilization.
